Our compile pins `addi rN,r1,108` (0x9c/0xa0 arm 1, 0x108 arm 2) to the LAST word of the loop preheader in every state measured, which is one slot later than the target - so the residual is now correctly stated as a BASE-position question, not a mask-position one, and the mask-position lever class is denied above. SHAPE B (the zero seed against the FixMLineText call, two sites): the target emits `@0x84 li r25,0` and `@0x144 li r22,0` in the gap between `addi r5,r1,108` (argument 3) and `add r3,r6,r0` (argument 1), i.e. inside the argument-setup run and two words after the `lwzx r0,r3,r0` that `add r3,r6,r0` consumes; ours emits both seeds after the `bl`. Read that way it is a load-use delay FILL - the target had the constant available to fill the two-cycle gap and we do not - which is scheduler-internal and consistent with the live-zero law. No build was spent on shape B this pass.

hypothesis.statement: The mask cannot be moved later, so the BASE must be moved earlier - the axis this function has never been probed on. Measured this pass: across the kept state, PROBE 6 and PROBE 7, ours emits `addi r23,r1,108` as the LAST word of the loop preheader in every state where the mask is not inside the loop (offsets 0xa0, 0x9c, 0xa0 respectively), whereas the target emits it SECOND-to-last at 0x9c with the mask at 0xa0. The base is the inlined call's `(u8**)buf2` argument, materialised lazily; the untried lever is to give it an earlier demand point - e.g. a file-local `u8** lines` assigned from `buf2` BEFORE the FixMLineText call at the CALL SITE (not in the helper), so the r1+108 address is already live when the inlined preheader is built. Note that `addi r5,r1,108` is ALREADY emitted at 0x80 as FixMLineText's own third argument in both streams, so the question is specifically whether a source-level shared web between that argument and the helper's `buf` parameter changes which of the two the allocator rematerialises - and whether it costs an instruction, which is the whole risk.
